fixes.explanation: Close, but the text says the opposite. The priests answer, “No,” replied the priests, and that's the ruling. The meat is consecrated, yet the food it touches does not become holy.

Holy is the word from the first question, where the priests said no. Here Haggai asks about someone defiled by contact with a corpse. The priests answer, “Yes, it becomes defiled…” So the food ends up defiled, not holy.

That's it. The LORD says, “Now consider carefully from this day forward: Before one stone was placed on another in the temple of the LORD…” He points them back to that moment before the first stone sat on another. Then He tells them what they saw from that time on.
Doors never come up here. The LORD says, “Before one stone was placed on another in the temple of the LORD…” So the time He means is before one stone sat on another. Nothing about shutting anything.

False is right. Someone came expecting a heap of twenty ephahs of grain and there were but ten. The winepress told the same story: someone came to draw out fifty baths and there were but twenty. Half a heap or less, and nobody likes that math.

The ark isn't mentioned in this passage. The LORD says that day is “…the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid…” That's the moment He wants them to look at. Nobody is carrying anything big through the door yet, so I'd keep the ark parked in the barn of our imagination.

Not yet, and that's exactly what the verse says. “The vine, the fig, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yet yielded fruit.” The LORD asks whether there is still seed in the barn, and He points out that these plants haven't yielded yet. Then He gives His promise. So the honest answer is false.
False, you got it. “The vine, the fig, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yet yielded fruit.” They haven't yielded yet. And then the LORD turns it around with a promise.

Bless is the word, and what a way to end. The LORD says, “But from this day on, I will bless you.” The barn question and the plants that have not yet yielded fruit come first, and then comes that promise. I think it's a good one to read twice.

Scatter isn't what He says, friend. After all those hard lines about thin harvests, I'd have braced myself too. But He says, “But from this day on, I will bless you.” That's a promise of blessing, and it starts from this day on.
